newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo tractor factory faces strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Yugo tractor factory faces strike threat.

text.p: An independent trade union in the Belgrade engine and tractor factory IMT on Tuesday threatened to strike in demand for back pay and in support of students demonstrating against the government.
Vidoje Scepanovic of the independent union Solidarnost (Solidarity) told Reuters the stoppage would begin on December 9 when a strike notice period expires.
Informed sources said 2,000 union members at the IMT plant had already unofficially stopped work in the dispute over non-payment of wages for five months.
IMT employs about 4,200 workers with average monthly wages of about 400 dinars ($80).

The Belgrade daily Dnevni Telegraf quoted union official Nebojsa Lazarevic as saying that police had threatened the workers if they attempted to leave the plant during working hours before the notice expires.
Scepanovic said Solidarnost supported opposition and student claims that the ruling socialists rigged local election results last month to deny the opposition victory.
The dispute has resulted in 16 days of street protests in Belgrade.
"We will respect provisions of the law and join the protests next Monday," Scepanovic said.
Serbia's united independent trade union Nezavisnost (Independence) has also called on its members to join the protests.
